column2: HERO — build the Claryo hero, a 10/10 reference that has never been attempted. OPEN design-refs/strips/Claryo_Ambient_Hero_Page.png before writing anything. The reference alternates WITHIN the hero between white technical line-work on full black and polished purple/steel imagery, and everything moves and settles cleanly. This is the model for what our hero becomes once a vertical is chosen. Do NOT clone it 1:1 - founder note: 'I do not think a 1 for 1 replication of this should be achieved, it is an example of a perfect hero page once a selection has been made.' HARD CONSTRAINT: §3 protects the hero demos (painting and equipment walls, their proximity engines and live metrics). They must stay the brightest and most detailed thing on screen and must not be made smaller, quieter or slower; tests/gimmicks.spec.ts will fail you if their timers break. The ambient field and venue wireframe already in the hero are founder-approved - build around them, do not replace them. Take a genuinely different approach from the other candidates in how the two registers alternate and what triggers it.

HERO STAT — build the PlayVision hero-stat layout, a 10/10 reference never attempted. OPEN design-refs/strips/Playvision_Video_and_Hero_Stat.png. Founder: 'there is a clean view of what the product demo video and Hero Stat looks like, the layout is perfect for what we want to recreate even if we do not have the video available yet.' So build the LAYOUT now with the video as a considered placeholder. §4d governs the slot and §7's placeholder addendum is explicit: a well-executed placeholder is NOT a deficiency and must not be scored as one - but §9 forbids any placeholder that implies footage exists which does not. No fabricated screen recordings, no stock passed off as product output. The hero stat must be a real, defensible number or clearly marked illustrative; §9 forbids fabricated results. Take a different approach from the other candidates on where the stat sits relative to the media and how the placeholder states its own emptiness.

SCROLL — finish the job against Claryo Scroll 1 and 2 (both 10/10); the founder says it is still not perfect. OPEN design-refs/strips/Claryo_Scroll_Functionality.png and Claryo_Scroll_Functionality_2.png and shots/best/motion/scroll.png. THREE MEASURED DEFECTS from the flow review, all yours to fix. (1) DEAD SCROLLS: content coverage across the nine scroll frames measures 81, 95, 56, 92, 43, 80, 33, 82, 54 percent. Frame 48% holds one unbroken empty band of 421 CSS px and frame 72% holds 299px. Both are register crossings (#how -> #value, #stack -> #use) where a closing pb-40/md:pb-52 pairs with an opening pt-40/md:pt-48, about 400px of content-free ground, and the seam's clamp(16rem,46vh,30rem) crossing lands inside that gap so the ground change gets a whole viewport to itself. Every scroll must surface something. (2) #value crosses register twice for no reason: it declares canvas between two technical sections (#how and #privacy), costing 403px of empty ramp in and 406px out for a section with only 489px of content - the crossings cost more page than the section does. (3) HowItWorks step 4 puts data-register=product on the CARD WRAPPER, so three light bordered cards are followed by a borderless black slab at the same radius, breaking the sequence device; the register belongs on the demo block inside the card, not the card. Also extend the header's register hand-off: it holds the root ground after selection, so it should observe the section currently beneath it and take that section's register. Take a different approach from the other candidate.
